title: Embankment on clay, no excess pore pressure (B-bar tutorial, step 1)

meta.title: Embankment on clay, no excess pore pressure (B-bar tutorial, step 1)
meta.notes: A 2 m embankment (crest x = 13–20.6 at y = 7, 1.5:1 faces to y = 5 at x = 10 and 23.6; γ = 20 kN/m³, c′ = 5 kPa, φ′ = 32°) on 1 m of upper clay (c′ = 10 kPa, φ′ = 20°) over 4 m of lower clay (c′ = 15 kPa, φ′ = 20°; both γ = 17 kN/m³), water table at the clay surface (y = 5), dry embankment; failure towards −x; circular search, Bishop simplified. Step 1: no excess pore pressure; the critical circle stays in the embankment.

source.reference: Tutorial of a commercial slope stability program: undrained loading by the B-bar method (its tutorial pages and the tutorial's project file).
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V104a (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Geometry, materials and water from the tutorial's project file (scenario "Master Scenario" of group 1); the FOS from the tutorial text ("FS = 2.30"). cSlope's circle (10.32, 8.70, R 3.70) is tangent to the embankment base, as the tutorial describes.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
